- Co-term the added capacity to your current renewal date so you only have one renewal cycle (Option A).
- Or run the top-up as a 12-month add-on with an independent start date (Option B); procurement sometimes prefers this structure.

We can support either billing approach but procurement asked for clarity on prorations and invoice timing. For transparency, rough costs below (net):
- Additional reserved pool (20 GPUs): $XXX,XXX/year
- One-time provisioning/setup: $X,XXX (if needed for region placement)

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min procurement call later this week to walk the amendment and billing options.

Regards,

Hi Liam —

Thanks — below are two clean options (we'll produce an amendment for whichever you prefer):

Option A (recommended, co-term):
- Add 20 GPUs into existing reserved pool immediately.
- Billing: prorated invoice covering the added GPUs for the remainder of current term (through 2027-08-31), then single co-termed renewal invoice at renewal.
- Benefit: single renewal cadence; lower admin overhead.

Option B (separate 12-month add-on):
- Add 20 GPUs with a fresh 12-month term starting on signing date.
- Billing: separate invoice schedule (we can do quarterly per your preference).

SLA & throughput: we will commit to a throughput SLO of 600 tokens/sec p90 for the additional capacity. We will also include an availability target for the dedicated pool and a rollback/fallback policy to lower-cost variants if capacity issues arise.

Requested items from your side to finalize the amendment:
- PO number (or a placeholder)
- Finance preference: prorated + co-term invoice OR separate quarterly invoices
- W-9 (we'll attach in the final DocuSign packet)

I've attached a draft PO amendment that uses Option A language (QS_PO_Amendment_Draft_v2.pdf). If you want quarterly billing we can toggle to Option B pricing in the doc and produce a line-item breakout.

Next step: would you and your finance lead be available for a 25-min touch on Friday 14th at 11:00am ET to confirm invoicing?

Best,
